clue.text: My word for doggie dish

definitions.note: an exclamation of surprise, a mild oath

indicators.note: to dish something is to wreck or spoil it, so the letters of the two words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming about what is in the dog's bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' looks like the bowl itself but works as a verb meaning ruin: rearrange FOR and DOGGIE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or dismay, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: Hangover chiefly to restrain incipient corpulence of the stomach

parts.note: read as hang over: hang is SAG, and over turns it round to give the three letters

indicators.note: chiefly points to the chief, leading letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: A cure for the morning after that keeps a paunch from starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangover' splits as hang (SAG) plus 'over', which turns it backwards; 'chiefly' takes the first letters of 'to restrain incipient corpulence', TRIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the stomach, as in gastric juices or a gastric ulcer.

clue.text: Urban work he investigates requires a desperate character

parts.note: OP is the standard abbreviation for opus, a work
a private investigator, a PI
Desperate Dan, the strongman of the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A city job for a detective calls for a reckless type.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a long-running cartoon cowboy in the British children's comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare adjective means belonging to a town, from Latin oppidum, a town.

clue.text: He gives away funnel for a cocktail

parts.note: a grass is an informer who gives people away to the police
a hopper is a funnel-shaped container that feeds material through

explanation.surface: Someone handing out a funnel to make a mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: GRASS is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy mint-green mixed drink of crème de menthe, crème de cacao and cream carries this name.

clue.text: 25 diamonds squandered, we hear

definitions.note: 25 down is a shade or colour, so this is one particular shade

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

indicators.note: we hear signals that the spoken word stands in for one spelt differently

parts.note: blew, as in blew all the money

explanation.surface: Jewels wasted, so rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' is the answer to 25 down, a colour word; this clue gives a pale colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A very pale, glacial blue is one particular shade, an instance of a colour.

clue.text: Vain search to include roundabout double parking

indicators.note: to include means the search word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: to fish is to search or grope for something
a roundabout is a circle, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: double asks for the letter from parking to appear twice

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A futile hunt for a space while double-parked at a roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' looks like futile, but it is the definition in its self-admiring sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandified and conceited, overly concerned with one's appearance, a synonym for vain.

clue.text: 25's not PM after leading close run election

definitions.note: 25 down is a colour, so this is one particular colour

indicators.note: after puts the morning abbreviation behind the other letters
leading picks the front letter of each of the three words that follow

parts.note: the opposite of PM (afternoon) is AM, morning

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister who is not in office after a tight election race.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, but 'not PM' is AM, morning rather than afternoon. 'leading' takes the first letters of 'close run election'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish off-white is a recognised colour name, an example of a shade.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge central role in public utility

indicators.note: central role in points to the letters at the very middle of the two-word phrase

explanation.surface: Snubbing the key part someone plays in a public service.
explanation.walkthrough: The three middle letters of PUBLIC UTILITY straddle the gap between the words.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone, ignoring them in the street, is to cut them dead.

clue.text: Title is abused by snob

indicators.note: abused means misused or mistreated, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A snob misusing an aristocratic title.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes in the superiority of a select few looks down on others, as a snob does.

clue.text: South African animal meat possesses a low rating

indicators.note: possesses means the first word holds the other one inside it

parts.note: taken as written
an erk is RAF slang for a low-ranking aircraftman or rating

explanation.surface: South African meat that gets a poor review.
explanation.walkthrough: ERK is old British forces slang for the lowest-ranking airman or sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: This small burrowing mongoose of southern Africa is a familiar example of an animal from that region.

clue.text: Opt out of apposite anagram 25

definitions.note: 25 down is a colour, so this is one particular colour

indicators.note: anagram openly says the letters are rearranged, once the other word has been taken out of them

explanation.surface: Choosing not to use a fitting word puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opt out of' tells you to remove O, P and T from APPOSITE; 'anagram' then shuffles the remaining APSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown tone named after cuttlefish ink, familiar from old photographs, is one particular shade.

clue.text: Understand pastime in which he's involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: the word he, with the 's acting as is

explanation.surface: Grasping a hobby that someone is caught up in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles PASTIME together with HE.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify with someone's feelings is to understand them in a deeper, sympathetic sense.

clue.text: Staff ends up agreed to differ

indicators.note: up tells you to read those final letters in the opposite direction
ends picks the final letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Employees finally settle on disagreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' takes D, O, R from 'agreed to differ', and 'up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick or pole, such as a fishing pole or measuring stick, is a staff.

clue.text: Hold out for one's viewpoint about life support

parts.note: split as view and point: the point is a compass point, south-east

indicators.note: about means scrambled, turned around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a stick is something to lean on, a support

explanation.surface: Standing firm in your view on life-support machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewpoint' does double duty: 'view' completes the definition (held out for one's view), while 'point' is a compass point. 'about' is the anagram signal, with no container needed.
explanation.definitionFit: This gadget is a pole held at arm's length so a phone camera can capture its owner's own view.

clue.text: Inferior editorial team member on London paper, briefly

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor, who checks copy on a newspaper

indicators.note: briefly means the paper's name is shortened, losing its first word

parts.note: the Evening Standard is London's evening newspaper

explanation.surface: A poor-quality subeditor working on a London newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the Evening Standard, London's evening newspaper, to its second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the expected level of quality, so not up to scratch: a synonym for inferior.

clue.text: Excuse when party's over

parts.note: Con is the abbreviation for the Conservative party
finished, done

explanation.surface: Making excuses once the celebration has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook or forgive an offence is to excuse it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A regular occurrence at one's home ground

parts.note: a habit is something done regularly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that happens routinely at your own home pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The natural surroundings where a plant or animal lives are its home territory.

clue.text: Used to 6 down various places listed to open

indicators.note: various suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters are arranged differently
to open asks for the letter that opens the word listed

explanation.surface: Instructions for cutting in several places on a list, to open them up.
explanation.walkthrough: '6 down' is CUT, so the definition reads 'used to cut'. 'various' rearranges PLACES as SCALPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small sharp knife is a tool for making incisions.

clue.text: Free impersonator loses remit for a particular voice

indicators.note: free means loosened, released, so the remaining letters are set free to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mimic stops imitating a certain singer's voice for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes R, E, M, I, T out of IMPERSONATOR; 'Free' rearranges the leftover PSONAOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest singing range, for women or boys, is a specific type of voice.

clue.text: Writer of article starts to lose heart after foreign agreement

indicators.note: after puts the two initials behind the French word

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
oui is French for yes

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: An author of a piece starts despairing after an overseas treaty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer of article' looks like a journalist; the definition is just 'Writer', a French playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Anouilh was a twentieth-century French dramatist, author of Antigone and Becket.

clue.text: Unions pass off workmates

indicators.note: off means the pass word is taken away from the front of the other

parts.note: colleagues are people you work with
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Trade unions deceive fellow workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass off' reads like deceive, but 'pass' is COL, removed from COLLEAGUES.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance or association of clubs or states is a league, so the plural fits unions.

clue.text: Revised Maastricht Treaty lacking chemistry — heard repeatedly from knockers

indicators.note: revised means altered or redrafted, so the leftover letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A redrafted European treaty missing its chemistry provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the letters of CHEMISTRY from MAASTRICHT TREATY; 'Revised' rearranges the rest, AATTRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase imitates the sound of repeated rapping on a door, which door-knockers make.

clue.text: Old clothing ripped without intention

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the torn word wraps round the other

parts.note: rent is an old past tense of rend, meaning torn
an aim is an intention

explanation.surface: Antique garments torn apart for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic or literary word for garments, dress, clothes in general.

clue.text: Shake like 16 down over first meeting

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the voice word sits around, covering the other letter

parts.note: 16 down is a high singing voice, and a treble is similarly a high voice

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word meeting is taken

explanation.surface: Quivering like a high voice at a first encounter.
explanation.walkthrough: '16 down' is SOPRANO; a boy soprano is a TREBLE, which goes round M.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver or shiver is to shake, verb for verb.

clue.text: Bastard to get retrained, once worn out

indicators.note: retrained means taught again, so the letters are put through a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A rotter is retrained, having once been exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' looks like exhausted; it means worn on the outside, as these tunics were over armour.
explanation.definitionFit: These short sleeveless tunics were historically worn over armour, on the outside.

clue.text: Erotica and porn rubbished by new generation

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed or wrecked, so the letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: Smut condemned by today's youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of producing offspring creates a new generation, a reproduction sense.

clue.text: Go out with Victorian female poet for starters

indicators.note: for starters keeps only the starting letter of each of the poet's three names

parts.note: Elizabeth Barrett Browning, the Victorian poet of Sonnets from the Portuguese

explanation.surface: Dating a nineteenth-century poetess, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Elizabeth Barrett Browning is the poet; 'for starters' takes her initials, not words in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide retreating is said to go out, the sense of this verb.

clue.text: Vitriolic Commons output of the '80s

parts.note: vitriol is sulphuric acid, so vitriolic means acid
the House of Commons, the lower house of the UK Parliament

explanation.surface: Bitter speeches produced in Parliament during the 1980s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' looks political: it is the House of Commons, Britain's lower chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of electronic dance music emerging in the late 1980s, a product of that decade.

clue.text: Part of 24 loses even tone

indicators.note: loses even means the letters in even positions, second and fourth, are dropped

parts.note: 24 across is a two-word music style; its second word is the part taken

explanation.surface: A section of a dance track drops its steady tone.
explanation.walkthrough: From HOUSE, 'loses even' drops the second and fourth letters, O and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour, shade or tint is a synonym for tone in the visual sense.

clue.text: 25's doctor taking part in a TV series

definitions.note: 25 down is a colour, so this is one particular colour

indicators.note: taking part in means the doctor letters sit inside the others

parts.note: ER is the American hospital drama series
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A colourful doctor appears in a television drama.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the American hospital drama; MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a crossword doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellowish-orange shade, like a traffic light's middle lamp, is one particular colour.

clue.text: Christ briefly implicated in opposite sides for 25

definitions.note: 25 down is a colour, so this is one particular colour

indicators.note: implicated in means the shortened name is caught up inside the side letters
sides points to the two outermost letters of the word opposite

parts.note: Chr. is a dictionary abbreviation for Christ

explanation.surface: Christ is drawn in by people on opposing sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposite sides' gives O and E, the two ends of OPPOSITE.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy yellow-brown pigment is one particular shade of colour.

clue.text: Incredibly end with assets in bloated condition

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something unbelievable, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: An unbelievable finish, with wealth leaving one feeling overfull.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely full after eating, glutted, is a state of bloating.
